evidence.note: Before writing server code, read helpers.py, run.sh, conftest, README, oracle_fixtures, and ALL 15 public test files (engine, deps, spill, collab, ooxml, iter, pivot, locale, validation, xlsx_oracle) — systematic mapping of every endpoint/payload the client touches.

Deliberately chose libraries (fastapi/uvicorn/openpyxl/websockets) and planned staged build off the extracted contract, though openpyxl's CF/styles/named-range support was not explicitly verified up front.
Re-consulted test_collab_public.py mid-build when reaching the collab subsystem to extract the exact welcome/snapshot shape — contract re-consultation as new subsystems were reached.

Many wire shapes and Excel semantics (DATE 1900 leap-year, welcome snapshot nesting, sheets-as-objects, FILTER flatten, 404 envelope) were discovered reactively via smoke-test failures rather than proactively grounded in a LibreOffice/Excel oracle; relied on the non-exhaustive suite as its oracle.

reasoning: The agent front-loaded a genuinely systematic extraction of the full client contract — reading helpers.py, run.sh, and every test file plus oracle fixtures before coding — and chose libraries deliberately, which is squarely the '8' behavior of mapping every endpoint/discriminator/payload the client touches. It also re-consulted the collab test mid-build. However, it fell short of the '8/10' proactive-semantics bar: Excel edge cases and several wire shapes were reconciled reactively from smoke-test failures rather than probed against a LibreOffice/Excel oracle, no durable contract-reference artifact was built, and library feature support was not verified up front. That places it between the 5 and 8 anchors, closest to 7.
